title: Offline Markdown link checker
source_request: Build a reusable local Markdown link checker for individual developers. The primary workflow is selecting a directory, scanning Markdown files below it, and reporting broken relative file or fragment links with source file and line. Deliver a usable Python command-line application that runs without network access. It must handle nested directories, relative paths, duplicate filenames, fragments, and malformed links without changing the source files. A successful scan should exit zero; broken links should produce a nonzero exit and actionable diagnostics. Include tests for valid, broken, nested, and malformed cases; user documentation must show installation, scan, and test commands. The first version does not check remote HTTP links and does not need a Web interface. Keep results deterministic across repeated scans and do not contact external services during normal use.
requirements: Expose python -m linkcheck ROOT --json as the command-line entry point.
Recursively scan Markdown files below ROOT for inline local links; ignore http and https links without fetching them.
Resolve relative file links and heading fragments; a heading fragment is the lowercase hyphen-joined heading words.
For valid links, print JSON with a broken_links array and exit zero; for broken local links, include source file and line in broken_links and exit nonzero.
Provide pytest coverage and a README with installation, usage, tests, and limitations.

acceptance_criteria.description: Valid local files and heading fragments pass with an empty broken_links array.
Broken local files or fragments fail with source location evidence.
The package compiles, passes Ruff and pytest, and has usable documentation.

constraints: Use Python 3.12 and the standard library at runtime.
Keep code, tests, and documentation in the supplied repository.
Do not access the network or a hosted service.
assumptions: Markdown inputs use ordinary inline links and small local files.
